notes.title: Qubicle 3.1.2 out now
notes.content:
Hey guys,
I have just uploaded the next version. Here's what's new:

[list]
[*] You can now set a target size for your Voxelizer. So instead of using scale you can exactly say how big you want your voxelization result. Voxelizer > Set Target Size
[*] I have made some minor tweaks to the workflow. You can now dbl-click to apply an extrude operation instead of using Enter. Same for drawing of standard primitives and box select
[*] You can now open the color mixer and set the tool colors without clicking on the color button but by using a keyboard shortcut. I have set it per default to C for primary and Shift+C for secondary. But you can of course change that to your linking. Tools > Set Primary/Secondary Color
[*] The Qubicle Binary QB export now offers an additional setting called "remove name index" which removes the name indices of exported objects. So instead of "Box_1" the name will be just "Box". This will come in handy when you use the Individual Export option
[*] I also fixed two bugs that slipped in with the new translation feature. Both were found in the landscape generator.
[/list]

Have fun!
Cheers
Tim

notes.title: Qubicle 3.1 out now!
notes.content:
Hey guys, happy belated new year!

I have set up a new version for you which is the first one to support German - and potentially a lot of other languages. If you like to help me translate Qubicle, I have created a GitHub for this matter. There are also rewards! Visit https://github.com/minddesk/QubicleLocalization

Furthermore Qubicle now offers quick help for all actions: just move your mouse over a menu item or button and Qubicle will display help in the status bar at the bottom. Most of the actions are linked to a corresponding detailed help page of the online documentation. Just press F1 and your browser will display the help. On OSX this feature is not available yet because I simply didn't know what key to assign. Is there a standard key for this on OSX? Please enlighten me and I will add it asap.

As always: have fun!
Cheers
Tim

Here's the complete list of changes:

* Qubicle now available in German
* Quick help for all menu entries displayed in status bar
* Online documentation linked for all menu entries with available help (Windows only)
* New Mirror Wall toggle and view properties
* Pop up dialogs can now be closed with ESC
* Duplicate Special now with rotation and scale
* Fixed Voxelizer mesh load bugs (spaces in filenames, Blender)
* Fixed DAE Export bug (added # for data references)
* Replaced all appearances of the word "swatch" with "color"

notes.title: We just expanded Qubicle's basic features!
notes.content:
The full range of modeling tools is now available in the basic application, making it even more powerful without additional DLC.

Qubicle basic now includes:
[list]
[*] All transform commands
[*] All modifiers (except compounds)
[*] Tool-mirroring symmetry
[*] All swatch tools
[/list]

Qubicle Utility DLC is now available for $10 instead of $20.

The Utility DLC enables:
[list]
[*] Use of compounds (object hierarchies)
[*] Height map import
[*] Random terrain generation
[/list]

Changes to the DLC setup will apply automatically with the new 3.0.6 update.
Thanks for helping us improve Qubicle and happy modeling!

notes.title: Coming up next
notes.content:
Hey guys,
after some (very much needed) days offs, I am back on track. This is what happens next.

Minor bug fixes/improvements
- Dbl-click file open (unsure if this is really fixable but I'll try)
- OS X render to file bug
- Season Pass label
- Minecraft block import issue (128 limit)
- Minecraft add cutom block
- Custom edge bleed size
- Mesh Export file naming for model (currently "model" should be qbcl file name)

Bigger issues
- T-junctions (difficult, will take some time)

The next big thing: New render engine

I started working on Qubicle 11 years ago, the way I render hasn't changed much over time. So, yes, Qubicle still uses the fixed function pipeline. I am changing it to programmable now. The new render engine should significantly improve render performance. Plus, it will feature perspective camera (FPS & Trackball), shadows, deferred lighting and more. This is just the groundwork for more... (having some plans)

If you've found more bugs, please post them in the discussion with info on how I can reproduce them. Thanks!

Cheers
Tim

notes.title: [UPDATED] The first 48 hours on Steam
notes.content:
Hey guys,

my name is Tim, I am the developer of Qubicle and founder of Minddesk. Qubicle is out on Steam for two days now and I am very thankful for all the feedback you gave. 
What really makes me happy is the fact that you seem to like my software and that some of you already started posting first models on the discussion boards. A big thank you to the community!

Furthermore I would like to thank you for your constructive feedback found in the reviews. It mostly adresses my decision to offer “Qubilce Voxel Editor” with the possibility to extend it with dlc.

Qubicle is available on the market for six years now and is used mostly by indie developers to make video games. Of course, they needed all the power and tools in the software to create beautiful designs for their games. But we also got a lot of requests, asking for an entry version at a lower price.

With the move offering Qubicle on Steam we wanted to give this possibility to those of you who are not game developers but just want a good and easy tool to create models in 3D.
At the same time our key interest is to still offer the full package to our steady customers - the indie developers. 

To accomodate those two things we decided to offer with “Qubilce Voxel Editor” an entry version that includes all the basic stuff you need to get started. Like import and export possibilites, direct upload to sharing and 3d-printing platforms, modding helpers for voxel games and most important all coming updates and fixes of the editor. We provide detailed info under the “About This Software” section on the shop page. 

I want to point out, that It was our main intention to offer Qubicle to a larger audience and not to to use dlc as a pricing strategy to generate maximum cash.

But your feedback showed me, that we have to be clearer  in communicating these aspects. That is why we will implement the following improvements:

1. We will offfer a Qubicle Indie bundle for $75 (regular price without discount) at the earliest possible date that will include all available dlc and all future dlc coming to Qubicle 3.0 

[UPDATE]
2. If you already own Qubicle Voxel Editor and want to upgrade to the Indie Bundle: we will provide a way to do that without paying more than if you would have ordered the Indie Edition in the first place
3. We will set-up a demo that will be fully usable for 10 days
4. Locked features are not shown in the basic application anymore

Not only in the last 6 years, also in the future I will take care of your feedback and your suggestions as it helps me improve Qubicle every day.

Cheers
Tim

notes.title: Qubicle 3.0.1 out now
notes.content:
Hey guys,
we've just uploaded a new version.
Based on early feedback we made following changes:

[b]Some features are unlocked now in the Basic app[/b]
Some reviews pointed out that some basic features are missing in the basic app. This is what's now unlocked:
- Arbitrary rotate/scale
- all tools
- export pivots can now be set/edited
- export to fbx, dae including all export options (except for mesh optimization which remains in the mesh dlc)

Owners of the utility module will get new features first to compensate this.

[b]locked features are now hidden[/b]
So you won't see any more padlocks. Our intention was to allow you to test features before you buy a dlc. We removed that. Instead we offer a Demo coming early next week.

We are looking forward to your feedback.
Cheers
Team Minddesk
